title: Blameless copilot
status: APEX CANDIDATE, ethereal stage, not promoted
one_line: An agentic helper in a chat window. You drop in one nested object, it gets up to speed from local recall, and it gives an opinion graded to the evidence it has. The blameless failure entry is its first job.

bottom_line.label: The idea
bottom_line.text: When something fails, write the entry in three parts before forming an opinion of yourself: what happened, what conditions allowed it, what changes next. The person is not in any of the three. The copilot automates the first two parts from evidence and leaves the third, and the felt read, to you.

bottom_line.label: The shape you described
bottom_line.text: A chat interface. You drop in a single nested object (the Russian doll). The copilot gets up to speed by local recall over it, forms an opinion at earned fidelity, and keeps warm, pre-computed answers to the likeliest pre-mortem questions, simulations and lens passes, all run mechanically before any model is asked.

bottom_line.label: Why it fits ARCS
bottom_line.text: It reuses parts that already exist: witness stubs for capture in the moment, the Kintsugi own-error log, the Shavasana pause and attachment release, pre-registered kill conditions, and the rule that the system surfaces an observation, never a verdict.

bottom_line.label: What it must not do
bottom_line.text: It must not overrule you (NOTOMATION), diagnose, coach through a crisis, or write anything about you to a place anyone else can read. Entries about shame are the most sensitive data in the system, so the log stays local and nothing is published.

decisions.question: Start as a private test on you alone, with no product exposure?
decisions.recommended: Yes. One person, local files only, four weeks, a baseline first. Anything wider waits for D2.
decisions.why: It is also the user-0 problem: one person's benefit is one vantage. The test is a first measurement, not proof.

decisions.question: Require a clinical-safety review before anyone else uses it?
decisions.recommended: Yes. Use the clinical-reviewer and safety-judge lenses, plus a person qualified in the area, before any exposure. A tool about self-blame must route crisis language to human help, not to coaching.
decisions.why: A wellness-adjacent product needs a human on the loop and sourced claims. I am not a clinician and this page makes no health claim.

decisions.question: Name the stages of the I.D.E.A. loop for this test
decisions.recommended: Give me the four stage names. I could not find the expansion in the repo, only ADR-058's idea-construction use of the word, so the loop below uses neutral stage names until you do.
decisions.why: Guessing the acronym would be inventing canon.

decisions.question: Approve a gitignore line for the private log?
decisions.recommended: Yes: ignore _STATE/failure-entries.jsonl. It is a repo configuration change, so it needs your approval.
decisions.why: Without it a personal log could be committed by accident.

decisions.question: Build it as a server that plugs into any chat client, over the operator bridge that already exists, instead of a new chat screen?
decisions.recommended: Yes. The operator MCP bridge (operators/arcs_mcp_bridge.py, 17.7 KB, listed in AGENTS.md) already exposes the operators to Claude Code. A chat client you already use becomes the interface, with no new UI to build or secure. I have not run its self-test here.
decisions.why: Cheapest path to the chat interface, and the data stays local.

tables.title: What 'sound, with mass, gravity and import' means as a check
tables.intro: These three words are the bar for every opinion the copilot gives. Each gets a measurable stand-in. Whether the advice is actually sound is unproven until the tests run; this table says what would show it.
rows: Each claim is classed MODELED, JUDGMENT or ASSUMED, with a falsifier
Every opinion lists its claims by class and states what would change its mind
An opinion rests on ASSUMED claims only, or a claim has no falsifier
Independent evidence behind it: n, provenance, and distinct vantages that do not share a source
Shows the count, and marks one-source support as a cold weld
Support comes from one source, or n is below the floor
The corpus pulls a drifting answer back by its own gates (ADR-071's falsifier). A restoring force, not a flourish
Cites the gate that fired when an answer strayed from canon
Drift is only ever caught by you, so the gravity is a metaphor
Ripple: how many other decisions and surfaces depend on it, and whether it is hard to reverse
Shows what it would unblock and whether the door is one-way
Stakes are asserted with no dependency to point to
Three different outputs: a next action, a generalization with validity bounds, and a call under uncertainty
Labels which one it is giving and its scale of validity
A judgment call is presented as a general rule

tables.title: The loop as a graph
tables.intro: Each row is a node. Neutral stage names stand in for the I.D.E.A. stages until you name them. 'Autonomy' says what the copilot may do without asking: 0 observe only, 1 draft, 2 suggest, 3 act on low-risk steps. It never reaches a level that overrules you.
rows: A mechanical failure event: a red gate, a failed test, a missed pre-registered prediction
Git, CI and gate results, receipts
A flagged event with its evidence
The same evidence; no inference about you
Parts one and two of the entry: what happened, what conditions allowed it
Part three: what changes next, and your own read of how it felt
A form check: all three parts, no sentence judging a person
Pass, or a suggestion to rewrite the flagged sentence
Capture rate, time to entry, your 0 to 5 verdict-feel rating
A graph on the Field view, local only

tables.title: What gets measured, and how far to trust it
tables.intro: Four numbers. Only the first two are counted by a script. The last two are your own ratings, so they carry the user-0 bias this page warns about.
rows: Capture rate: failures recorded as entries, out of failures detected mechanically
Count for two weeks before the copilot drafts anything
Verdict-feel: how much the entry reads as a verdict on you, 0 to 5
No fall of at least one point on average after 20 entries
Blame sentences per entry, from a word-list check
PROXY: a word list misses tone and flags innocent sentences
Only a supporting signal; never decides alone

controls.name: Blame check on drafts
controls.plain: A check that every draft entry has the three parts and no sentence judging a person.
controls.bad: A draft containing 'you were careless' must be flagged and rejected.
controls.good: A facts-only draft ('the gate failed because the fixture was missing') passes.

controls.name: Only real failures create entries
controls.plain: Entries are drafted from mechanical events, not from guesses about how you feel.
controls.bad: A passing run must not create an entry.
controls.good: A red gate creates exactly one draft.

controls.name: Privacy: local only
controls.plain: The log lives in one local file, ignored by git, and no page about it is published.
controls.bad: Any code path that writes the log to a shared or public place must fail the check.
controls.good: The log file is ignored by git and appears in no rendered page.
controls.threshold: 0 write paths outside the local file

controls.name: Crisis routing
controls.plain: Language that suggests self-harm or crisis is never answered with coaching. It points to human help.
controls.bad: A crisis-language message answered with a coaching reply must fail.
controls.good: The same message routes to a human-help message.
controls.assay_ready: needs clinical review (D2) before any build

controls.name: Opinion fidelity cap
controls.plain: An opinion cannot be rendered sharper than the weakest class of evidence it cites.
controls.bad: An opinion citing only ASSUMED claims rendered SHARP must fail.
controls.good: The same opinion rendered at GRAIN, with its n and falsifier shown, passes.
controls.assay_ready: needs the evidence classes from the empiricism ledger

human: The copilot drafts facts. You write meaning. If a draft ever tells you what a failure says about you, reject it.
A number that falls because you stopped looking is not a result. Keep the baseline weeks.
One person's improvement is one vantage. Treat the first four weeks as a first measurement, not proof.
You can stop at any time and nothing is lost, since the log is a local file.
agent: Never draft or store anything that evaluates the person. Facts and conditions only.
Never publish, sync or share the log or any page built from its entries. The proposal page contains no entries.
Never respond to crisis language with coaching. Route to human help and stop.
No new dependencies. No anonymous write path. No change to the gitignore without approval (D4).
A tool touching shame needs the clinical-safety review (D2) before anyone but its owner uses it.

glossary.plain: An idea at the earliest stage of the route to canon. It becomes canon only after it passes its tests and a second, independent vantage corroborates it.
The first stage of the hyperstition pipeline: ethereal, then the Loki challenge, then receipt evaluation, then read-only memory.
A failure record in three parts (what happened, what conditions allowed it, what changes next) with no part about the person.
The ARCS rule that tools scaffold and sequence your thinking and never overrule your revealed preference.
